text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: High ECC/IO error rate observed on gpu-host-02 (us-central1). Multiple inference tasks evicted. Investigate.
maria_oncall: I'm on it. Affected pool: dedicated-prod-gpu. Noting customer impact: degraded throughput for a subset of requests, some 5xx spikes on /generate routes.
sam_infra: I see node gpu-host-02 flapping, reprovision attempts failed. nvme errors in syslog. Pushing dmesg and kernel logs to the thread.
raj_ops: Added temporary traffic-split to fallback model pool (dedicated-prod-gpu-b). Routing 30% away from the node. Will increase if errors persist. @maria_oncall please confirm SLA impact.
maria_oncall: customers with reserved capacity might see slightly longer tails; no full outages yet. Escalating to Sev-2.
jen_prodeng: Can someone dump `nvidia-smi -q` and ECC totals? Also need PCIe AER logs.
sam_infra: Pasting recent kernel excerpt:
```
[drm] Uncorrectable ECC error on GPU 1
pci 0000:65:00.0: AER: Multiple Uncorrected errors detected
nvme nvme0: completion timeout
```
sam_infra: `nvidia-smi -q` snippet: ECC errors increasing on GPU1, memory errors count jumped by 120 in last 10m. KV cache eviction spikes in runtime logs.
lee_sre: Hypothesis 1: hardware ECC degradation on GPU1. Hypothesis 2: PCIe link flapping due to host firmware bug. Hypothesis 3: noisy neighbor causing NVMe saturation leading to host stalls and timeouts.
raj_ops: I've opened a support ticket with GCP. Ticket 123456789: possible PCIe AER and NVMe timeouts. Sharing the ticket link: https://console.cloud.google.com/support/tickets/123456789
maria_oncall: Mitigations: cordon gpu-host-02, drain running pods with `kubectl drain gpu-host-02 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`, then reprovision or move to spare host.
sam_infra: Starting drain now. ETA ~2m for live tasks to migrate (we have graceful shutdown=10s). If evictions happen during drain we'll abort and fallback more traffic.
incident-bot: [action] On-call handover recorded: maria_oncall -> raj_ops in 30m if unresolved.
jen_prodeng: Can we get traces for a failing request? I want the per-token latency and which model variant was hit. Also attach `perf` flame for the process if possible.
sam_infra: Uploaded profiler dump and runtime logs to /shared/incidents/1981234567/profiler.tar.gz
lee_sre: Adding timeline so far:
- T+0:00 pager triggered by ECC/NVMe alerts
- T+2m: first customer 5xx spike observed on /generate
- T+4m: nvme errors appear in kernel log
- T+7m: ECC counts rising on GPU1
- T+10m: cordon/drain started; fallback routing 30%
raj_ops: Observed one host reboot during reprovision attempt (likely kernel panic). Rebooted automatically, but errors resumed after ~3m.
jenn_prodeng: (typo) jen_prodeng: noted. If reboot recovers briefly then issues return, that points at hardware or firmware persistent fault.
maria_oncall: Short term plan: keep node cordoned, increase fallback to 60%, and open maintenance window for sustained reprovision. Notify customers in #support-status.
sam_infra: I'll trigger full node reprovision (replace host). If reprovision fails, we'll retire the host from pool and reallocate capacity.
lee_sre: For RCA notes: collect `dmesg`, `lspci -vvv`, `smartctl` for NVMe, `nvidia-bug-report.sh`, and PCIe AER counters. Tag logs with correlation id 1981234567.
gcp-alerts: GCP: Noted device 0000:65:00.0 reported AER uncorrectable error, kernel OOM work observed. Recommended: host reboot, firmware check.
raj_ops: I'll coordinate with GCP support for firmware/BIOS and host-level NVMe diagnostics. Also asking for host migration history to see if this node had previous transient errors.
jen_prodeng: Action items captured: 1) gather full logs (sam), 2) reprovision/replace host (sam), 3) escalate to GCP for firmware (raj), 4) update customers + postmortem owner (maria).
maria_oncall: I'll own the postmortem. Please drop any additional evidence or timelines into /shared/incidents/1981234567/pm_notes.md.
sam_infra: Drain completed, workloads moved. Reprovision started. If reprovision fails we'll rotate physical host out.
lee_sre: Next hypothesis to rule out: NVMe firmware causing timeouts — if smartctl shows failing sectors or high reallocated sectors we treat as root cause. If not, PCIe link or ECC module failure.
raj_ops: Keeping ticket with GCP open; they requested a `sysrq` log collected at time of kernel oops — uploaded.
incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Update: node drained and reprovision initiated by sam_infra. Monitoring post-migration for 15m. On-call: raj_ops.
maria_oncall: Thanks all. Keeping channel open for RCA coordination. If anyone finds smoking-gun evidence, paste it here. :mag:
lee_sre: Quick note: one customer reported partial content corruption on embeddings job around T+5m — including that in the impact section for the PM. Possible data retransmit needed on affected requests.
sam_infra: Reprovision completed successfully. Running health checks. ECC counters stable now on replacement host. Closing immediate mitigation.
maria_oncall: Marking incident as mitigated. We'll continue RCA collection and postmortem. Closing pager for now. :slightly_smiling_face:
